text: This course started with two stakeholders asking for two different things, and ended with a real production incident, diagnosed and fixed. Here's the whole shape of it, start to finish, and where it leads next.

It opened with the ask growing: the retail chain's Store Ops team and its Regional Manager each needed numbers the original pipeline didn't cleanly support. That led to a deliberate incremental design, planned before a single line of new code got written. Bronze ingestion switched to picking up only new files, and Silver got upserted with a real Delta Lake merge, correctly matched on transaction_id, the one column actually guaranteed unique. Then came both Gold tables, daily_sales_summary for Store Ops and category_breakdown for the Regional Manager, and the reconciliation query from Lesson 9 that proved the two of them agreed.

From there, Power BI connected both tables to the people who'd asked for them, store ops got its page, the regional manager got theirs. Then a real bug surfaced: a later maintenance change swapped the merge's match key to store_id and sale_date, which isn't unique, and the two gold tables quietly stopped agreeing. That bug was reproduced against real data, isolated to the exact date it started, confirmed with describe history and a controlled count query, fixed by restoring transaction_id, and proven fixed by re-running the exact same reconciliation query.

That five-step method is the real takeaway, more than any single query. Reproduce the report with a known tool, against real data, before touching anything. Isolate one variable to see exactly where a symptom starts and stops. Confirm the actual cause with a controlled test that returns real evidence. Fix the smallest thing that's actually wrong. Then re-validate with the same diagnostic tool that caught the problem, so fixed means proven, not assumed. That sequence outlives this specific bug completely.

This course was the Intermediate Project, one pipeline, one incremental redesign, one real bug, worked all the way through. The next, bigger step in this path is the Data Engineering Career and Capstone course, a full eighty-one lesson, four chapter program that builds on everything covered here, incremental pipelines and merge-based upserts included, through career-readiness work and a complete capstone project of its own. If this course felt like real work, that one is the next, larger version of exactly that.
